newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-ENGLAND AND ITALY POISED FOR WARY WARM-UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLAND AND ITALY POISED FOR WARY WARM-UP.

text.p: One thing is certain about the England-Italy clash at the Beaujoire Stadium on Wednesday -- it will bear no resemblance to their subsequent meeting in Rome in October.

The Tournoi de France game is likely to be a cagey confrontation featuring two experimental line-ups, with managers Glenn Hoddle and Cesare Maldini careful to give nothing away before their final World Cup qualifier.

England vastly improved their chances of reaching the World Cup finals with a thoroughly professional 2-0 win over Poland in Chorzow on Saturday. It would be fair to say they are approaching the Tournoi de France in a serious, but relaxed mood.

Hoddle hinted he might try a 4-4-2 formation and play David Beckham in a central midfield role rather than wide on the right. He may also play Gareth Southgate as a sweeper and bring Philip Neville in as one of the fullbacks.

"I would gladly have swapped a win in Poland for three defeats in this tournament," said Hoddle, "but we are greedy so now we want to win the games over the next week too. We are going to France to be professional. That's what it is about. It is not going to be relaxed as you might think, but the win against Poland has certainly taken the pressure off."

Maldini has to juggle with an injury-hit and fatigued squad which has just finished the serie A season. He may well leave his son and team captain Paolo out of the starting line-up against England to give the defender more time to fully recover from injury.

"I have to take account of those in bad shape, starting with my son Paolo who has not yet recovered from his latest injury and will probably only be available for the second match, against Brazil on Sunday," Maldini was quoted as saying in Gazzetta dello Sport.

Antonio Bennarivo of Parma is considered the most likely replacement at left back. The Parma defender was a regular in the national squad which made it to the World Cup final in 1994 but has not played recently due to injury.

Midfielder Alessandro Del Piero, a last-minute inclusion in the squad who looked doubtful after he was hit in the face by a ball in the European Cup final last week, is also unlikely to start against England.
Del Piero, who has not played international soccer for most of this year after receiving a thigh injury in February, is still not fully match fit.

In attack, Chelsea's Gianfranco Zola looks set to partner experienced Lazio striker Pierluigi Casiraghi. Coach Maldini is without Fabrizio Ravanelli and Roberto Baggio, who scored in his international comeback last month. Both are injured.

Defender Alessandro Costacurta and midfielder Demetrio Albertini should play, although Maldini has said he wanted to use the tournament to test replacements for the two who are both suspended for the next World Cup qualifier against Georgia.
Maldini admitted he does not really want to take part in a tournament held so close to the end of an exhausting domestic season but said Italy would still take it seriously.

"When you come up against England, Brazil and France, you don't just go to look at the view as if you were on holiday," he said. "Everyone says the results don't matter at the beginning but then if we lose it will be like the end of the world."

The teams may be announced late on Tuesday after final training or early on Wednesday. England (possible): David Seaman; Gary Neville, Gareth Southgate, Sol Campbell, Phil Neville, Paul Ince, David Beckham, Robert Lee, David Batty, Teddy Sheringham, Alan Shearer Italy (probable): Angelo Peruzzi, Ciro Ferrara, Antonio Benarrivo, Fabio Cannavaro, Alessandro Costacurta, Dino Baggio, Angelo Di Livio, Dimetrio Albertini, Roberto Di Matteo, Filippo Casiraghi, Gianfranco Zola.
